findings.issue_text: [BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher's matchesSafely returns false exactly when the grant shortcut matches the expected value, inverting the assertion. Every event assertion using isAccessTokenId (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) fails for correct token IDs ('ac:uuid' returns false) and would pass for tokens with the wrong grant type, so the test helper validates the opposite of its intent and breaks all dependent integration tests.

[BUG] The matcher reads the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5), but the encoded layout is sessionType(2 chars)+tokenType(2 chars)+grantType(2 chars), so the grant shortcut occupies substring(4, 6). The matcher compares a window straddling the last char of tokenType and the first char of grantType (e.g. for 'acrtac' it compares 'rt'), so even with the inverted logic fixed it never inspects the actual grant type and the assertion is meaningless for its stated purpose.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") for the rawTokenId check instead of Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...), a copy-paste that leaves rawTokenId unchecked. A null rawTokenId is accepted by the constructor and only surfaces later as 'null' text inside the encoded token id (e.g. 'acrtcc:null'), producing malformed token IDs and a misleading error message when grantType (not rawTokenId) is the null value being reported.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the public Context(Context) copy constructor and simultaneously adds an abstract getShortcut() to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface, which are silent breaking changes to public SPI surface for out-of-tree grant implementations. Third-party providers implementing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory fail to compile/load after upgrade (no default method for getShortcut), and any code that relied on the copy constructor breaks; existing custom grants deployed as jars now throw AbstractMethodError at runtime when Keycloak calls getShortcut().

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the encoded context before the first ':' to be exactly 6 characters, but nothing constrains an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory's getShortcut() to 2 characters, and the interface javadoc only says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. A custom grant deployed with a 1- or 3-character shortcut (explicitly permitted by the loose contract) produces token IDs the decoder rejects with 'Expected length of 6', so all access tokens issued via that grant become undecodable by this provider.

[BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher is doubly broken: substring(3, 5) reads the wrong characters (grant shortcut occupies indices 4-6, so it compares tokenType's last char + grant's first char), and the comparison logic is inverted (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns no-match when the grant IS correct). The grant-shortcut assertion never fires: for a correct token id like "onrtac:<uuid>" the matcher extracts "ta", which never equals "ac", so it falls through to the UUID check and passes. The renamed grant assertion is a silent no-op, so a regression that drops the grant-type encoding in token IDs would not be caught by any test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken.

[BUG] The constructor contains a duplicated null-check: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` is applied to grantType instead of rawTokenId, so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId is accepted by construction and later surfaces as an NPE (or the string "null" is embedded in the encoded token id, e.g. "onrtcc:null") in TokenManager.initToken, producing malformed token IDs instead of a fail-fast contract violation as the check intends.

[ADVISORY] Adding the abstract getShortcut() method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface with no default implementation breaks source and binary compatibility for every out-of-tree custom OAuth2 grant provider. Deployments with custom grant-type extensions fail at deploy/compile time after upgrading, with no migration note in the diff; the risk is that a broken custom grant also breaks the whole TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException) and takes token issuance down with it.

[ADVISORY] The public copy constructor Context(Context context) is silently deleted from the Context API surface with no deprecation cycle. Any extension code (custom grants that wrapped an existing Context, e.g. token-exchange-style delegation) that called this constructor fails to compile after upgrade; the diff also leaves no replacement for the shallow-copy use case since no copy method was added.

[ADVISORY] The only new test bypasses the factory's real registration path: it hand-populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts with two entries and never calls postInit, and no test in the diff exercises DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, the lazy map-refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut, or an end-to-end issued token ID. Regressions in postInit (e.g. duplicate-shortcut detection, custom grant registration) or in the lazy-refresh fallback used when a grant provider is deployed after startup go completely unverified; the integration surface (TokenManager.initToken producing prefixed jtis from a real token endpoint request) is only covered by the isAccessTokenId matcher, which is itself a no-op due to the inverted-logic bug.

[ADVISORY] encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when the client-session's grant type has no registered shortcut (e.g. an admin-configured or future grant path that never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE and whose value does not fall into the 'na' fallback), turning token issuance into a 500. Any token-issuing path in the diff that calls createClientAccessToken without setting the GRANT_TYPE attribute and whose formParams grant value is a non-standard string (client-supplied grant_type values reaching OAuth2GrantTypeBase via custom providers) hits the hard failure at TokenManager.initToken instead of degrading to the UNKNOWN encoding, breaking token issuance for that flow.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and a wrong substring index, so it never matches any token ID and every assertion using it fails. matchesSafely returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected value (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), i.e. it rejects the exact case it is supposed to accept; additionally substring(3,5) reads characters 4-5 (sessionType's second char + tokenType's first char) instead of the grant shortcut at positions 4-6 per the code's own comment, so even with the inversion fixed it checks the wrong slice and expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions either always fail or validate nothing.

[BUG] The constructor null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted. `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` is a copy-paste error; encodeTokenId then produces a token ID ending in the literal string ":null" for any caller passing a null rawTokenId, and later getTokenContextFromTokenId will hand back that corrupted ID as the raw token id instead of failing fast.

[ADVISORY] The public copy constructor `Context(Context)` is deleted while `Context` remains a public API in server-spi-private, breaking source compatibility for out-of-tree OAuth2GrantType implementations. Any third-party or Keycloak-internal grant that constructed a derived Context via the copy constructor fails to compile against this version, and the replacement single-arg constructor also adds a new behavior (reads grantType from formParams) not present before; this is a silent public-surface change with no deprecation cycle, biting custom grant authors on upgrade.

[ADVISORY] The PR titled as a context-encoding framework unconditionally changes the format of every access token's jti from a bare UUID to a 6-char-prefixed composite ID, with no feature flag or compatibility path in the diff. This is implementation work beyond the stated 'framework' scope that alters the externally observable token ID format for all clients and all grant types at once; any consumer (admin event filtering, external systems, stored jti values used for revocation lookups keyed on the old format) sees a different ID shape with no option to disable it, and tokens issued before the change decode through the UNKNOWN fallback branch on refresh — the diff contains no test asserting that a pre-existing plain-UUID token id round-trips through validateToken, so this invariant is not enforced.

[ADVISORY] The duplicated-shortcut validation in postInit only compares map sizes, so it does not detect a grant whose shortcut collides with an existing grant's ID or an ID colliding with a shortcut, and it silently overwrites entries on collision. If two OAuth2GrantTypeFactory deployments share a shortcut, `grantsByShortcuts.put` overwrites one of them and both maps can still end up the same size (e.g. one grant's shortcut equals another's full ID), so the guard passes, a deployment starts, and getTokenContextFromTokenId later decodes the wrong grant type for tokens issued by the overwritten grant — a hot-path correctness failure with no error at startup despite the code claiming to validate it.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId's matching logic is inverted and reads the wrong character positions: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns 'no match' exactly when the grant shortcut matches. The encoded context is 6 chars (e.g. "onrtac"): grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5, but substring(3,5) reads indices 3-4 ("ta"), so the grant is never actually verified; and because equality is negated, a token whose chars 3-4 happen to equal the expected grant shortcut is declared a non-match while any other value falls through to the UUID check and passes. The matcher is a stand-in guard that passes for arbitrary grant types and fails for the one arrangement it names, so every expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertion green-lights tokens with wrong grant encoding.

[BUG] The diff deletes the public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` from the OAuth2GrantType.Context SPI class. API-CONTRACT-BREAKING-CHANGES: the class is in server-spi-private and consumed by grant implementers (e.g. device/CIBA grants historically construct a derived Context and call setFormParams on it); removing the public constructor breaks compilation of every out-of-tree OAuth2GrantType extension and any in-tree call site not shown in this diff, and replaces a field-complete copy with a formParams-reading constructor whose behavior differs (see stale-grantType finding).

[BUG] The constructor null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` CONFUSABLE-PAIR: a null rawTokenId is accepted silently while a null grantType produces a misleading message claiming rawTokenId was null; consumers encoding a context built without an id (e.g. from a parse path) produce tokens with a null id segment instead of failing fast at the boundary the check was written for.

[ADVISORY] initToken changes the public shape of the access-token `jti` claim from a bare UUID to a 6-char prefix + ':' + UUID (e.g. "onrtac:<uuid>") for every token issued by every realm. Unversioned breaking contract change for external consumers: clients, resource servers, audit pipelines, and DB columns/regex validators that assume jti is a 36-char UUID break on upgrade; the reverse-path getTokenContextFromTokenId handles legacy ids, but nothing in the diff handles downstream consumers of the new format. Any admin/realm that disabled the encoding via a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider still pays the SPI indirection on every token mint.

[ADVISORY] grantType is snapshotted once in the constructor from formParams, but the class still exposes setFormParams() which can replace the form params afterwards without updating grantType. Callers that build a Context and then swap in different form params (the pattern the deleted copy-constructor was used for, e.g. device grant building a derived context) get a stale grantType baked into the access token's jti prefix, so the encoded context misreports the grant that actually produced the token — exactly the drift the encoder exists to prevent.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation compares map sizes after already having overwritten entries: `grantsByShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN)` collides with any real grant whose getId() or getShortcut() is literally "na", and size-inequality only detects collisions in one direction. Two deployed grant factories sharing a shortcut silently overwrite each other in grantsByShortcuts while both remain in grantsToShortcuts — the size check catches that case, but a shortcut collision against the reserved "na" sentinel is masked by the sentinel put happening after the loop, so an extension using shortcut "na" silently encodes/decodes as UNKNOWN and the postInit 'validation' still passes.

[ADVISORY] The encoded format hardcodes a 2-char fixed-width field for the grant shortcut and a total context length of 6 chars, enforced by a magic literal with no named constant shared with the encoder. Two parallel representations of the layout: TokenContextEncoderProvider implementers and the AssertEvents matcher each hardcode offsets/lengths independently (the matcher already got substring(3,5) wrong); a future change to field width or order desynchronizes every custom encoder and parser at once, and any custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a shortcut longer or shorter than 2 chars produces a context that decode rejects with IllegalArgumentException on tokens it just issued — the constraint is not enforceable at the interface where it is defined.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown 6-char contexts, but the map-population fallback in the factory only helps for grants whose factory is currently deployed in this server. In a cluster with heterogeneous deployments, or when introspecting/validating a token whose grant was produced by a since-undeployed custom grant provider, decode throws IllegalArgumentException on a token the system itself minted; the parse API offers no UNKNOWN fallback for the grant field the way it does for the no-prefix legacy case, so the caller-visible behavior differs between 'old token' (parses to UNKNOWN) and 'token with a now-unknown grant' (hard exception).

[ADVISORY] The refresh path unconditionally overwrites the client session's GRANT_TYPE attribute with REFRESH_TOKEN, destroying the original grant that produced the session. Every access token obtained via refresh reports grant 'rt' regardless of whether the session originated from authorization_code, password, or device grant — any downstream consumer or admin tooling distinguishing 'what grant bootstrapped this session' gets a rewritten value on refresh, and the original is unrecoverable since the attribute is in-memory state not persisted to the client session notes.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId has an inverted match condition plus an off-by-one slice: it returns false exactly when the grant shortcut matches, and it reads substring(3,5) instead of the grant-type's actual position substring(4,6). Every expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertion passes only for tokens whose jti grant shortcut does NOT match the expected grant, and fails for correctly-encoded tokens; the test harness silently validates the wrong behavior, so a regression that encodes the wrong grant type into the token id would not be caught and existing correct behavior is reported as broken.

[BUG] The constructor null-checks grantType twice ("Null grantType not allowed" then "Null rawTokenId not allowed" on grantType again), so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId is accepted and later rendered as the literal string "null" after the ':' in encodeTokenId, producing token ids like "onrtcc:null" that parse back to the string "null" instead of failing fast; the intended invariant the message names is silently not enforced.

[ADVISORY] The public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted outright rather than deprecated, and the new grantType field is populated only in the surviving constructor (from formParams), so any copy-constructed Context would have missed it anyway. Third-party OAuth2GrantType implementations in server-spi-private's consumer surface (custom grants compiled against the previous constructor) fail to load at deploy time with NoSuchMethodError after this change, with no deprecation cycle to signal the break.

[ADVISORY] validateToken overwrites the client session's Constants.GRANT_TYPE with OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN unconditionally, discarding whatever grant the session originally recorded. After any refresh, an access token minted via a cross-session flow records grant "refresh_token" rather than the original grant, so getTokenContextFromTokenId reports a grant type that differs from the grant that actually authenticated the user — consumers of the encoded context get silently rewritten provenance; the diff changes observable token-id content on every refresh path without a documented decision that refresh replaces rather than preserves the original grant.

[BUG] encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered shortcut, breaking token issuance for any third-party OAuth2GrantType deployment. Keycloak supports custom OAuth2GrantType providers deployed as JARs; OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is a new interface method third-party factories don't implement (returns null or a duplicate), so factory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null and initToken() in TokenManager now throws during createClientAccessToken — every token request for clients using that grant returns a 500 instead of a token, a hard availability regression the previous code did not have.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5), but the encoded context places the grant shortcut at indices 4-5 (chars 5-6), so the matcher compares the wrong two characters. For a token id like 'onrtac:uuid' the matcher reads 'rt'+'a'[3:5]='ta' wait — substring(3,5) yields chars at index 3 and 4, i.e. the last char of tokenType plus first char of grantType ('ra' for a regular/auth-code token), never matching the expected grant shortcut; tests either always fail or pass only when tokenType's second char coincidentally equals the check, masking wrong token ids from the CODE_TO_TOKEN/REFRESH_TOKEN event assertions the diff was meant to strengthen.

[ADVISORY] The token id (jti) now discloses session persistence state (online/offline/transient), token format (regular vs lightweight), and grant type to any holder of the access token. jti is a public JWT claim visible to resource servers and anyone who captures the token; internal deployment details (e.g. that a session is transient, that lightweight tokens are enabled, that a user authenticated via password grant vs client credentials) are now broadcast where they previously were opaque UUIDs; an attacker profiling tokens can fingerprint realm configuration from the outside.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher has both an inverted boolean and an off-by-one index, so it rejects every correctly-encoded token id and passes only malformed ones. `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false exactly when the grant shortcut matches — the condition is inverted (should return true) — and the comment says the 2-char grant shortcut starts at the 4th character but substring(3,5) extracts characters at indices 3-4 (e.g. for 'trltac' it yields 'ta', not 'ac'). Every test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken fails against correctly issued tokens, and would pass against a token whose grant-type segment is garbage, so the matcher verifies the opposite of the new encoding behavior.

[ADVISORY] The isAccessTokenId matcher only checks the grant-type segment and the UUID tail, never the session-type or token-type segments the diff introduces. An integration regression that mis-encodes SessionType (e.g. offline tokens encoded as 'on') or TokenType (lightweight vs regular) in the token id passes every event assertion in the suite; whoever refactors DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider gets no signal that the first four characters of jti changed.

[ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException and asserts nothing about its type or message, so it passes on any runtime failure the code throws for any reason. If getTokenContextFromTokenId starts throwing IllegalStateException or an unrelated NPE before reaching the intended validation, the test still passes; the specific 'unknown grant type shortcut' rejection path is never pinned to IllegalArgumentException, so a regression that replaces the intended error with a different one goes undetected.

[ADVISORY] The test hand-seeds the factory's grant maps, bypassing postInit, so the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation, the real grant registry, and both dynamic map-refresh branches in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut are never exercised. postInit's duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException guard and the dynamically-deployed-grant refresh paths (which dereference sessionFactory that the test leaves null) ship untested; a broken postInit that corrupts the maps or a refresh path that NPEs on late-deployed grant providers reaches production undetected. Also, testIncorrectGrantType uses shortcut 'ac' (authorization code) which IS registered in the real factory — it only throws because the hand-made map omits it, making the test verify the fake registry rather than the real behavior.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only production path that builds the encoded context from a live session — has no test anywhere in the diff; the sole test class DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest never references it (checked: it only calls getTokenContextFromTokenId and encodeTokenId). The sessionType derivation (TRANSIENT vs isOffline vs ONLINE) and the null-grantType fallback to UNKNOWN in the code path TokenManager.initToken now invokes on every token issuance are unverified; a regression that maps offline sessions to ONLINE or NPEs on a null persistence state breaks token ids for all real logins while the unit suite stays green.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring indices, so it asserts the opposite of its intent. `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) exactly when the grant shortcut IS correct, and the substring also grabs char at index 3-4 instead of the 4-5 where the 2-char grant shortcut lives (prefix is 6 chars: st+tt+gt). The matcher only passes tokens with the WRONG grant type, so the new encoding is completely unverified by the testsuite; a regression that misencodes grant types would still go green.

[BUG] Adding an abstract getShortcut() method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface breaks binary compatibility for every existing third-party grant implementation and turns their deployment into a hard startup failure. Any already-compiled custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (a supported extension point, since this lives in server-spi-private but grants are pluggable via META-INF/services) throws AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut(); because postInit runs at server bootstrap, the entire Keycloak instance fails to start, not just the custom grant — an upgrade with no migration path for custom grants.

[BUG] Removing the public copy constructor Context(Context) is a silent breaking change to the grant SPI's public surface. Custom grant implementations that construct Context via the copy constructor fail with NoSuchMethodError at runtime when the upgraded Keycloak (with this diff) loads them — a rolling deploy that includes custom grant extensions crashes on first use of the grant, with no compile-time signal for the operator.

[ADVISORY] The access-token jti silently changes from a bare UUID to a 7+ char prefixed form with no migration/compatibility handling for stored or external consumers of TOKEN_ID. Admins and monitoring pipelines that treat Details.TOKEN_ID as a UUID (the testsuite itself asserted isUUID() before this diff, proving that was the contract) now receive values like 'onrtac:uuid' and fail to parse them; during a rolling deploy, tokens minted by new pods flow to old pods and to event/siem consumers that assumed the UUID format, breaking correlation with no error surfaced by Keycloak itself.

[ADVISORY] The constructor validates grantType twice ('Null rawTokenId not allowed' is a copy-paste of the grantType check), so a null rawTokenId is accepted. A null rawTokenId slips through the guard and later produces the encoded token id 'xx x x:null' or NPEs downstream in encodeTokenId concatenation, producing a malformed jti in issued access tokens instead of the intended fast-fail at construction.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation compares map sizes, which does not actually detect colliding shortcuts when IDs also collide and never detects two grants sharing one shortcut plus another pair sharing an ID. If two grant factories return the same shortcut but different IDs (or vice versa in the reverse pairing), one silently overwrites the other in grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and the size check passes, so tokens get encoded with the wrong grant type and decode to the wrong grant — a silent data-fidelity corruption that the guard was written to prevent; the trigger is deploying any two custom grants with colliding shortcuts.

[BUG] The constructor's fourth null check validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` appears after the earlier grantType check. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted by the constructor (invariant violation), and when it is rejected the error message names the wrong field ('Null rawTokenId not allowed' fires for a null grantType), misdirecting debugging of token-encoding failures on the token endpoint.

[BUG] encodeTokenId concatenates the grant shortcut without verifying it is exactly 2 characters, while getTokenContextFromTokenId (line 82) hard-rejects any encoded context whose length is not exactly 6. A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a shortcut of length != 2 (e.g. "uma" or "c") produces tokens whose JTI encodes fine but whose context can never be decoded — every getTokenContextFromTokenId call on those tokens throws IllegalArgumentException, an encode/decode asymmetry that surfaces as runtime failures in whatever consumer later parses the token id, with no check at issuance time to catch it early.

[ADVISORY] postInit blindly calls grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName) on a ConcurrentHashMap without null-checking gtf.getShortcut(), so a custom grant factory returning a null shortcut (the new interface method is implemented but returns null) throws NullPointerException during factory postInit. Deploying one misbehaving custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory turns a per-request failure into a hard whole-server startup failure — Keycloak will not boot for any realm, rather than failing just the offending grant's requests.

[ADVISORY] initToken now calls encoder.encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException for any grantType whose shortcut cannot be resolved, turning every token-issuance path into one that 500s when the Constants.GRANT_TYPE client-session attribute holds an unregistered grant name. Any code path (custom SPI, token exchange to external/other-protocol subjects, or a persisted client-session attribute from a since-undeployed grant) that sets GRANT_TYPE to a value with no OAuth2GrantTypeFactory causes a raw 500 on the token endpoint instead of a degraded-but-successful token (the old behavior, plain UUID id), because the UNKNOWN fallback only applies when the attribute is null, not when it is unresolvable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the encoded context before the first ':' to be exactly 6 characters, but nothing constrains an OAuth2GrantTypeFactory's getShortcut() to 2 characters, and the interface javadoc only says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut'. However OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() (new SPI method) has no constraint that the shortcut must be exactly 2 characters; its javadoc even suggests it is “usually like 3-letters”. If a custom grant factory returns a 1- or 3-character shortcut, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() will emit an encoded context whose length is not 6, and the decoder will reject it with “Expected length of 6.” This makes tokens issued via such a grant undecodable by this provider, which is a real behavioral defect in the diff-introduced encoding/decoding contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher is doubly broken: substring(3, 5) reads the wrong characters (grant shortcut occupies indices 4-6, so it compares tokenType's last char + grant's first char), and the comparison logic is inverted (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns no-match when the grant IS correct). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when the client-session's grant type has no registered shortcut (e.g. an admin-configured or future grant path that never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE and whose value does not fall into the 'na' fallback), turning token issuance into a 500. adjudication.rationale: In the diff, missing GRANT_TYPE does fall back safely: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() reads clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, String.class) and if null assigns UNKNOWN ("na"). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() explicitly registers UNKNOWN in both grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts, so encodeTokenId() will not throw for flows that never set GRANT_TYPE. For flows that do set GRANT_TYPE, the value comes from OAuth2GrantType.Context (formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)) and the factory mapping is populated from all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances (which now must implement getShortcut()), so a registered/custom grant type should have a shortcut and be encodable. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR titled as a context-encoding framework unconditionally changes the format of every access token's jti from a bare UUID to a 6-char-prefixed composite ID, with no feature flag or compatibility path in the diff. This is implementation work beyond the stated 'framework' scope that alters the externally observable token ID format for all clients and all grant types at once; any consumer (admin event filtering, external systems, stored jti values used for revocation lookups keyed on the old format) sees a different ID shape with no option to disable it, and tokens issued before the change decode through the UNKNOWN fallback branch on refresh — the diff contains no test asserting that a pre-existing plain-UUID token id round-trips through validateToken, so this invariant is not enforced.

There is no feature flag or opt-out shown. That is an externally observable compatibility/architecture concern grounded in the diff, not a directly provable correctness bug. However, parts of the finding overreach: refresh/validateToken in this diff does not decode an old UUID `jti` via `getTokenContextFromTokenId`, and there is at least a unit test covering parsing of an old token id (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testOldToken`), though it doesn’t assert end-to-end behavior through `validateToken`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The duplicated-shortcut validation in postInit only compares map sizes, so it does not detect a grant whose shortcut collides with an existing grant's ID or an ID colliding with a shortcut, and it silently overwrites entries on collision. If two OAuth2GrantTypeFactory deployments share a shortcut, `grantsByShortcuts.put` overwrites one of them and both maps can still end up the same size (e.g. one grant's shortcut equals another's full ID), so the guard passes, a deployment starts, and getTokenContextFromTokenId later decodes the wrong grant type for tokens issued by the overwritten grant — a hot-path correctness failure with no error at startup despite the code claiming to validate it.

adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, a true duplicate-shortcut across *different* grant IDs will overwrite an entry in `grantsByShortcuts` but will still insert two distinct keys into `grantsToShortcuts`, making the map sizes differ and triggering the startup `IllegalStateException` (so it is not “silent”). The example mentioned (a shortcut colliding with another grant’s full ID) does not by itself overwrite either map (keys are `shortcut` vs `grantName` respectively), and does not cause `getTokenContextFromTokenId` to decode the “wrong” grant type. The only way collisions could keep sizes equal is if both the shortcut *and* the ID collide (e.g., duplicate implementations with the same ID and shortcut), which the finding does not establish from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId's matching logic is inverted and reads the wrong character positions: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns 'no match' exactly when the grant shortcut matches. The encoded context is 6 chars (e.g. "onrtac"): grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5, but substring(3,5) reads indices 3-4 ("ta"), so the grant is never actually verified; and because equality is negated, a token whose chars 3-4 happen to equal the expected grant shortcut is declared a non-match while any other value falls through to the UUID check and passes. The matcher is a stand-in guard that passes for arbitrary grant types and fails for the one arrangement it names, so every expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertion green-lights tokens with wrong grant encoding.

adjudication.rationale: The new `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId` matcher is incorrect as shown in the diff. It returns `false` when the (mis-sliced) substring equals `expectedGrantShortcut` (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), which inverts the intended logic. Additionally, the encoded context is 6 chars where grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 (per `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`: `gtShortcut = encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`), but the matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, checking the wrong characters. As written, it effectively doesn't validate the grant shortcut and can let wrong encodings pass, breaking the correctness of the updated event assertions (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, etc.).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] initToken changes the public shape of the access-token `jti` claim from a bare UUID to a 6-char prefix + ':' + UUID (e.g. "onrtac:<uuid>") for every token issued by every realm. Unversioned breaking contract change for external consumers: clients, resource servers, audit pipelines, and DB columns/regex validators that assume jti is a 36-char UUID break on upgrade; the reverse-path getTokenContextFromTokenId handles legacy ids, but nothing in the diff handles downstream consumers of the new format. Any admin/realm that disabled the encoding via a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider still pays the SPI indirection on every token mint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the access token ID generation in `TokenManager.initToken`: it no longer sets `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` but instead always calls `TokenContextEncoderProvider encoder = session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class); ... token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx));`, where `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` produces a 6-character context prefix plus `':'` plus the raw UUID. That is a real, diff-grounded externally visible contract change for the token `jti` value (and tests were updated to expect a non-UUID format in events). However, the finding’s downstream-breakage concerns are about compatibility/documentation/rollout rather than an internally verifiable correctness defect in the diff itself, so it’s best classified as an important non-bug review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] grantType is snapshotted once in the constructor from formParams, but the class still exposes setFormParams() which can replace the form params afterwards without updating grantType. Callers that build a Context and then swap in different form params (the pattern the deleted copy-constructor was used for, e.g. device grant building a derived context) get a stale grantType baked into the access token's jti prefix, so the encoded context misreports the grant that actually produced the token — exactly the drift the encoder exists to prevent.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, `grantType` is captured once in the constructor (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`) but `setFormParams(...)` remains and only replaces `formParams` without recomputing `grantType`. The new code paths then use `context.getGrantType()` to set `ClientSessionContext` attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)`), which feeds into access token ID encoding (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)`). If any caller mutates form params after construction via `setFormParams`, the encoded token context can reflect a stale grant type relative to the actual `formParams` in use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation compares map sizes after already having overwritten entries: `grantsByShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN)` collides with any real grant whose getId() or getShortcut() is literally "na", and size-inequality only detects collisions in one direction. Two deployed grant factories sharing a shortcut silently overwrite each other in grantsByShortcuts while both remain in grantsToShortcuts — the size check catches that case, but a shortcut collision against the reserved "na" sentinel is masked by the sentinel put happening after the loop, so an extension using shortcut "na" silently encodes/decodes as UNKNOWN and the postInit 'validation' still passes.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), a real grant factory using shortcut "na" would typically be detected by the existing size-based validation: the loop adds an entry for shortcut "na" to grantsByShortcuts, then the subsequent grantsByShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN) overwrites it (no size increase), while grantsToShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN) adds a new key "na" (size increases). This makes grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(), triggering the IllegalStateException. Also, the claim that the size check “only detects collisions in one direction” is incorrect: duplicate shortcuts shrink grantsByShortcuts while grantsToShortcuts keeps both entries, and duplicate IDs shrink grantsToShortcuts while grantsByShortcuts keeps both—both cases produce a size mismatch. While there is a theoretical edge case if a grant ID is literally "na" too, the finding’s stated silent-pass behavior is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The encoded format hardcodes a 2-char fixed-width field for the grant shortcut and a total context length of 6 chars, enforced by a magic literal with no named constant shared with the encoder. Two parallel representations of the layout: TokenContextEncoderProvider implementers and the AssertEvents matcher each hardcode offsets/lengths independently (the matcher already got substring(3,5) wrong); a future change to field width or order desynchronizes every custom encoder and parser at once, and any custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a shortcut longer or shorter than 2 chars produces a context that decode rejects with IllegalArgumentException on tokens it just issued — the constraint is not enforceable at the interface where it is defined.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces (1) a real parsing/validation defect in AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(): it uses substring(3,5) and also inverts the expected-grant check (`if (..equals(..)) return false;`), so it will reject valid token IDs produced by the new encoder (grant shortcut should be at indices 4..6 in the 6-char context). Additionally, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hardcodes `encodedContext.length() != 6` and splits the 6 chars into 2/2/2, but OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() does not enforce 2-char shortcuts (its javadoc even suggests “3-letters”), so a custom factory returning a non-2-length shortcut could yield token IDs that the decoder would reject with IllegalArgumentException.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown 6-char contexts, but the map-population fallback in the factory only helps for grants whose factory is currently deployed in this server. In a cluster with heterogeneous deployments, or when introspecting/validating a token whose grant was produced by a since-undeployed custom grant provider, decode throws IllegalArgumentException on a token the system itself minted; the parse API offers no UNKNOWN fallback for the grant field the way it does for the no-prefix legacy case, so the caller-visible behavior differs between 'old token' (parses to UNKNOWN) and 'token with a now-unknown grant' (hard exception).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does implement the described behavior: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId parses 6-char contexts and throws IllegalArgumentException when factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(gtShortcut) returns null (unknown grant shortcut), while the legacy no-prefix case returns UNKNOWN ("na"). The factory fallback only refreshes mappings from currently deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations; if none match, it remains null and decoding hard-fails. However, this appears intentional per the new test testIncorrectGrantType() expecting a runtime exception for an unknown grant shortcut ("ac"), so it’s more of a robustness/backward-compat/cluster heterogeneity concern than a clearly unintended defect per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refresh path unconditionally overwrites the client session's GRANT_TYPE attribute with REFRESH_TOKEN, destroying the original grant that produced the session. Every access token obtained via refresh reports grant 'rt' regardless of whether the session originated from authorization_code, password, or device grant — any downstream consumer or admin tooling distinguishing 'what grant bootstrapped this session' gets a rewritten value on refresh, and the original is unrecoverable since the attribute is in-memory state not persisted to the client session notes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the refresh path setting `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN);` in `TokenManager.validateToken(...)`, and token IDs are now encoded using `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` via `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` and `TokenManager.initToken(...)`. So refreshed access tokens will encode the `refresh_token` grant shortcut ("rt") regardless of how the session was originally created, and the original grant is not preserved anywhere in this diff (it is only stored as a `ClientSessionContext` attribute). However, whether this is a *defect* is not verifiable from the diff: the new constant/comment explicitly says it’s the “token grant type used”, which for refresh is plausibly intended to be `refresh_token` rather than the bootstrap grant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] validateToken overwrites the client session's Constants.GRANT_TYPE with OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN unconditionally, discarding whatever grant the session originally recorded. After any refresh, an access token minted via a cross-session flow records grant "refresh_token" rather than the original grant, so getTokenContextFromTokenId reports a grant type that differs from the grant that actually authenticated the user — consumers of the encoded context get silently rewritten provenance; the diff changes observable token-id content on every refresh path without a documented decision that refresh replaces rather than preserves the original grant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TokenManager.validateToken(...)` explicitly doing `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN);` right before recreating the access token, and the new token ID encoding logic uses `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (via `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` and `TokenManager.initToken`), so a refreshed access token will encode the refresh grant shortcut regardless of any prior value. However, the diff also updates tests to expect the refresh shortcut in token IDs (`AssertEvents.expectRefresh(...).detail(TOKEN_ID, isAccessTokenId(RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT))`), indicating this is likely an intentional semantics/observability change rather than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered shortcut, breaking token issuance for any third-party OAuth2GrantType deployment. Keycloak supports custom OAuth2GrantType providers deployed as JARs; OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is a new interface method third-party factories don't implement (returns null or a duplicate), so factory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null and initToken() in TokenManager now throws during createClientAccessToken — every token request for clients using that grant returns a 500 instead of a token, a hard availability regression the previous code did not have.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (no default implementation). Any third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` built against the previous interface would not implement it, and this code now calls `gtf.getShortcut()` during `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()`, which would fail for such deployments (e.g., `AbstractMethodError`/startup failure). Additionally, token issuance now depends on having a registered shortcut: `TokenManager.initToken()` always encodes the token ID via `encodeTokenId()`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` throws `IllegalStateException` when `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(grantType)` returns null. There is no fallback to `UNKNOWN` when a grant type exists but has no shortcut mapping. This creates a real availability regression for custom/extension grant types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5), but the encoded context places the grant shortcut at indices 4-5 (chars 5-6), so the matcher compares the wrong two characters. For a token id like 'onrtac:uuid' the matcher reads 'rt'+'a'[3:5]='ta' wait — substring(3,5) yields chars at index 3 and 4, i.e. the last char of tokenType plus first char of grantType ('ra' for a regular/auth-code token), never matching the expected grant shortcut; tests either always fail or pass only when tokenType's second char coincidentally equals the check, masking wrong token ids from the CODE_TO_TOKEN/REFRESH_TOKEN event assertions the diff was meant to strengthen.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the matcher parses the prefix before ':' (expected 6 chars: 2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grant shortcut per DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()). The grant shortcut should be extracted with substring(4, 6), but the diff uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which spans the last char of tokenType and first char of grantType, so it compares the wrong 2 characters. Additionally, the equality check is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the match when it equals the expected shortcut. Both issues make the assertion incorrect and can cause tests to fail or to not validate the intended grant shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The token id (jti) now discloses session persistence state (online/offline/transient), token format (regular vs lightweight), and grant type to any holder of the access token. jti is a public JWT claim visible to resource servers and anyone who captures the token; internal deployment details (e.g. that a session is transient, that lightweight tokens are enabled, that a user authenticated via password grant vs client credentials) are now broadcast where they previously were opaque UUIDs; an attacker profiling tokens can fingerprint realm configuration from the outside.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes AccessToken `jti` from an opaque UUID to an encoded string that includes session type, token type, and grant shortcut: `TokenManager.initToken()` now builds an `AccessTokenContext` and sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` returns `sessionTypeShortcut + tokenTypeShortcut + grantShort + ':' + rawTokenId`. This makes those attributes observable to any JWT holder/resource server. However, the change appears intentional (new SPI explicitly documents encoding context into token ID), so it’s a concrete design/security consideration rather than a clear correctness defect shown by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher has both an inverted boolean and an off-by-one index, so it rejects every correctly-encoded token id and passes only malformed ones. `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false exactly when the grant shortcut matches — the condition is inverted (should return true) — and the comment says the 2-char grant shortcut starts at the 4th character but substring(3,5) extracts characters at indices 3-4 (e.g. for 'trltac' it yields 'ta', not 'ac'). Every test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken fails against correctly issued tokens, and would pass against a token whose grant-type segment is garbage, so the matcher verifies the opposite of the new encoding behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant-shortcut extraction is wrong for the new 6-char context format (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantType). The grant segment should be at indices 4..6, but the matcher uses substring(3, 5), which mixes the last char of tokenType with the first char of grantType. Additionally, the boolean is inverted: `if (…equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the token exactly when the (mis-extracted) shortcut equals the expected value, so the matcher does not actually validate that the encoded token id contains the expected grant shortcut (it will typically accept IDs where it *doesn't* match).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The isAccessTokenId matcher only checks the grant-type segment and the UUID tail, never the session-type or token-type segments the diff introduces. An integration regression that mis-encodes SessionType (e.g. offline tokens encoded as 'on') or TokenType (lightweight vs regular) in the token id passes every event assertion in the suite; whoever refactors DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider gets no signal that the first four characters of jti changed.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher only splits on ':' and then (attempts to) validate a 2-char segment plus the UUID tail; it does not assert anything about the first four characters of the encoded context (sessionType + tokenType). So a regression where DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes the wrong SessionType (on/of/tr) or TokenType (rt/lt) would still satisfy these event assertions. This is a concrete test-coverage gap introduced alongside the new 6-char token-id context format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException and asserts nothing about its type or message, so it passes on any runtime failure the code throws for any reason. If getTokenContextFromTokenId starts throwing IllegalStateException or an unrelated NPE before reaching the intended validation, the test still passes; the specific 'unknown grant type shortcut' rejection path is never pinned to IllegalArgumentException, so a regression that replaces the intended error with a different one goes undetected.
matched_golden_ids: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points out that the test catches generic RuntimeException and would pass for any runtime failure, and specifically notes it should be pinned to IllegalArgumentException. This matches the golden issue about overly broad exception catching and needing to catch IllegalArgumentException instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test hand-seeds the factory's grant maps, bypassing postInit, so the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation, the real grant registry, and both dynamic map-refresh branches in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut are never exercised. postInit's duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException guard and the dynamically-deployed-grant refresh paths (which dereference sessionFactory that the test leaves null) ship untested; a broken postInit that corrupts the maps or a refresh path that NPEs on late-deployed grant providers reaches production undetected. Also, testIncorrectGrantType uses shortcut 'ac' (authorization code) which IS registered in the real factory — it only throws because the hand-made map omits it, making the test verify the fake registry rather than the real behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` does hand-seed `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` in `before()` and never calls `postInit(...)`, so the real `postInit` population from `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` and its duplicate-shortcut guard (`if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) throw ...`) are not exercised. Likewise, the dynamic refresh branches in `getShortcutByGrantType(...)` / `getGrantTypeByShortcut(...)` dereference `sessionFactory`, but the test constructs the factory without setting `sessionFactory`, and no test triggers those refresh branches. Also, `testIncorrectGrantType` uses shortcut `ac` (`"ofrtac:5678"`), but the diff adds `AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returning `"ac"`; it only throws in the test because the hand-made maps omit `ac`, so the test validates the fake registry rather than real factory behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only production path that builds the encoded context from a live session — has no test anywhere in the diff; the sole test class DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest never references it (checked: it only calls getTokenContextFromTokenId and encodeTokenId). The sessionType derivation (TRANSIENT vs isOffline vs ONLINE) and the null-grantType fallback to UNKNOWN in the code path TokenManager.initToken now invokes on every token issuance are unverified; a regression that maps offline sessions to ONLINE or NPEs on a null persistence state breaks token ids for all real logins while the unit suite stays green.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a new production path in TokenManager.initToken that always calls TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...) to derive sessionType/tokenType/grantType for the encoded token id. The only new unit test class (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest) exercises getTokenContextFromTokenId and encodeTokenId, but never calls getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, so the logic that maps UserSessionModel persistence/offline state to AccessTokenContext.SessionType and the null grantType fallback to UNKNOWN in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext is untested in this diff. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring indices, so it asserts the opposite of its intent. `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false (no match) exactly when the grant shortcut IS correct, and the substring also grabs char at index 3-4 instead of the 4-5 where the 2-char grant shortcut lives (prefix is 6 chars: st+tt+gt). The matcher only passes tokens with the WRONG grant type, so the new encoding is completely unverified by the testsuite; a regression that misencodes grant types would still go green.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the matcher logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects exactly the case where the grant shortcut matches the expectation, so it will only match tokens with a *different* shortcut. Additionally, the substring indices are inconsistent with the new token-id encoding introduced in this diff (`sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantType(2)` => grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, i.e. `substring(4,6)`, not `substring(3,5)`). This makes the tests fail to actually verify correct grant-type encoding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Adding an abstract getShortcut() method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface breaks binary compatibility for every existing third-party grant implementation and turns their deployment into a hard startup failure. Any already-compiled custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (a supported extension point, since this lives in server-spi-private but grants are pluggable via META-INF/services) throws AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut(); because postInit runs at server bootstrap, the entire Keycloak instance fails to start, not just the custom grant — an upgrade with no migration path for custom grants.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface. Any already-compiled implementation (e.g., a custom/provider JAR built against the previous interface) will not have this method and will throw `AbstractMethodError` when invoked. The new code in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, which runs during `postInit` (bootstrap). That makes the server fail to start if such an old binary is present, matching the finding’s core claim about hard startup failure due to binary incompatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the public copy constructor Context(Context) is a silent breaking change to the grant SPI's public surface. Custom grant implementations that construct Context via the copy constructor fail with NoSuchMethodError at runtime when the upgraded Keycloak (with this diff) loads them — a rolling deploy that includes custom grant extensions crashes on first use of the grant, with no compile-time signal for the operator.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previously available public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (it existed and is now deleted). Since `Context` is a `public static` type and the constructor was public, this is a binary-incompatible change: any already-compiled custom grant/provider code that invokes `new Context(existingContext)` will fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError` when loaded against this version. That runtime breakage is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The access-token jti silently changes from a bare UUID to a 7+ char prefixed form with no migration/compatibility handling for stored or external consumers of TOKEN_ID. Admins and monitoring pipelines that treat Details.TOKEN_ID as a UUID (the testsuite itself asserted isUUID() before this diff, proving that was the contract) now receive values like 'onrtac:uuid' and fail to parse them; during a rolling deploy, tokens minted by new pods flow to old pods and to event/siem consumers that assumed the UUID format, breaking correlation with no error surfaced by Keycloak itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the access token ID format from a bare generated ID to a context-prefixed form: `TokenManager.initToken()` now builds an `AccessTokenContext` and sets `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, where `encodeTokenId` returns `<6-char-context> + ':' + <rawTokenId>` (e.g., `onrtac:uuid`). The testsuite was updated accordingly (e.g., `AssertEvents` switched from `isUUID()` to `isAccessTokenId(...)`), which supports the finding’s claim that the prior implicit contract was UUID-shaped. The diff does include limited backward handling for parsing old token IDs without `:` (`getTokenContextFromTokenId` returns UNKNOWN context), but it does not show any explicit compatibility/migration story for external consumers that treat `Details.TOKEN_ID` as a UUID. That’s a real, diff-grounded backward-compatibility/API-contract concern, but not a directly verifiable correctness defect within the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The constructor validates grantType twice ('Null rawTokenId not allowed' is a copy-paste of the grantType check), so a null rawTokenId is accepted. A null rawTokenId slips through the guard and later produces the encoded token id 'xx x x:null' or NPEs downstream in encodeTokenId concatenation, producing a malformed jti in issued access tokens instead of the intended fast-fail at construction.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` is a copy/paste error and does not validate `rawTokenId` at all (`rawTokenId` can be null). This is directly visible in `AccessTokenContext.java`. If a null `rawTokenId` is ever passed, construction will not fail as intended and `encodeTokenId()` will concatenate `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, yielding a malformed token id ending in `:null` (string concatenation, not necessarily an NPE).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation compares map sizes, which does not actually detect colliding shortcuts when IDs also collide and never detects two grants sharing one shortcut plus another pair sharing an ID. If two grant factories return the same shortcut but different IDs (or vice versa in the reverse pairing), one silently overwrites the other in grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and the size check passes, so tokens get encoded with the wrong grant type and decode to the wrong grant — a silent data-fidelity corruption that the guard was written to prevent; the trigger is deploying any two custom grants with colliding shortcuts.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), duplicate detection is only `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())` after populating two maps via `put()`, which silently overwrites on collisions. While a single collision on shortcut or ID will usually change sizes and be detected, the size-equality check can miss combined collisions (e.g., two grants share a shortcut, and a different pair share an ID), yielding equal map sizes (both reduced by 1) and therefore no exception, despite incorrect/ambiguous mappings. That can lead to wrong shortcut<->grantType resolution during encode/decode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor's fourth null check validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` appears after the earlier grantType check. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted by the constructor (invariant violation), and when it is rejected the error message names the wrong field ('Null rawTokenId not allowed' fires for a null grantType), misdirecting debugging of token-encoding failures on the token endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null checks are incorrect: after checking `grantType` once (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed")`), it repeats the same variable again for the raw token id check (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`) instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected, and a null `grantType` could trigger the misleading message about `rawTokenId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] encodeTokenId concatenates the grant shortcut without verifying it is exactly 2 characters, while getTokenContextFromTokenId (line 82) hard-rejects any encoded context whose length is not exactly 6. A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a shortcut of length != 2 (e.g. "uma" or "c") produces tokens whose JTI encodes fine but whose context can never be decoded — every getTokenContextFromTokenId call on those tokens throws IllegalArgumentException, an encode/decode asymmetry that surfaces as runtime failures in whatever consumer later parses the token id, with no check at issuance time to catch it early.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), the encoded JTI is built as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort + ':' + rawId, but there is no validation that grantShort is exactly 2 characters. In contrast, getTokenContextFromTokenId() requires the pre-colon encodedContext to have length exactly 6 and then slices grant shortcut as substring(4, 6). Therefore, any OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation returning a shortcut length != 2 (the interface comment even suggests “3-letters shortcut”) will generate token IDs that cannot be decoded and will trigger IllegalArgumentException when parsed, creating an encode/decode asymmetry visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postInit blindly calls grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName) on a ConcurrentHashMap without null-checking gtf.getShortcut(), so a custom grant factory returning a null shortcut (the new interface method is implemented but returns null) throws NullPointerException during factory postInit. Deploying one misbehaving custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory turns a per-request failure into a hard whole-server startup failure — Keycloak will not boot for any realm, rather than failing just the offending grant's requests.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit, the code iterates all OAuth2GrantType factories and does `String grantShortcut = gtf.getShortcut(); grantsByShortcuts.put(grantShortcut, grantName);` with `grantsByShortcuts` being a `ConcurrentHashMap` (which rejects null keys/values). There is no null-check or fallback if a factory returns null for the new `getShortcut()` method, so a misbehaving/custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory can trigger an NPE during server `postInit`, i.e., at startup rather than per-request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] initToken now calls encoder.encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException for any grantType whose shortcut cannot be resolved, turning every token-issuance path into one that 500s when the Constants.GRANT_TYPE client-session attribute holds an unregistered grant name. Any code path (custom SPI, token exchange to external/other-protocol subjects, or a persisted client-session attribute from a since-undeployed grant) that sets GRANT_TYPE to a value with no OAuth2GrantTypeFactory causes a raw 500 on the token endpoint instead of a degraded-but-successful token (the old behavior, plain UUID id), because the UNKNOWN fallback only applies when the attribute is null, not when it is unresolvable.

adjudication.rationale: In TokenManager.initToken(), token.id is now always set via encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() only falls back to UNKNOWN when Constants.GRANT_TYPE is null; if it is non-null but not resolvable to a shortcut, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null and encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException ("Cannot encode token with unknown grantType"). There is no catch/fallback to the prior UUID-only behavior, so any path that sets clientSessionCtx attribute Constants.GRANT_TYPE to an unregistered value will cause token issuance to fail with a 500.
